F3. THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN GATE REJECTS F2's CLAIM WHEN IT IS PHRASED DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS HOW I KNOW THE FINDING IS NOT A MATTER OF TASTE. scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py carries a pattern at line 338, PR\s*#?\d+\s+is\s+(?:still\s+)?open, whose entire purpose is to refuse an open-PR assertion written into tracked prose. MUTATION PROBE M3, run on this tree: I rewrote the PR's own sentence as 'PR #29 is still open' and changed nothing else --
    $ python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .
    FAIL: HANDOFF.md:28: [open-PR assertion (PR #N is (still) open)] PR #29 is still open
    1 volatile state claim(s) ... EXIT 1
The identical assertion, as the PR actually words it ('...also open.'), passes: my unmodified run of the same command on this head prints only the timestamp UNVERIFIABLE line and exits 0. So the diff makes a claim the gate is built to reject and is saved only by word order. The gate's rule is not merely 'the claim must be true' -- it is 'do not assert volatile PR state in prose at all; use a live command or a volatile-ok escape'. This diff does assert it, and falsely.

== TWO NEAR-MISSES I CAUGHT AND AM PRINTING, AS THE ROUTINE REQUIRES ==

N1. I NEARLY CHARGED THIS PR WITH A DANGLING PROOF REFERENCE. proof/43.json names "commit": "3509d2f", and git cat-file -t 3509d2f in this clone returns 'fatal: Not a valid object name'. The commit a0f9481 states as its reason for leaving the field alone that the sha is 'unaffected by which PR lands it', which read to me like a false rationale after three re-cuts. Before writing it up I measured the base rate across every record in proof/: ALL 22 have a commit field that fails to resolve in this clone, because main's history is squash-merged and no pre-merge sha survives. 3509d2f also resolves fine through the REST API (it is the pre-recut form of this branch's b224d1b). So the field is house-normal and the rationale is correct. Charging it would have been an innocent-PR accusation; I withdrew it.

N2. I NEARLY CHARGED THIS PR WITH DELETING A LIVE RED CHECK. The diff removes item 1's sentence recording that main's tip '#34, NOT green: lwb-proof-coverage fails (#34 shipped with no proof/34.json, not in proof/exempt.json)'. I confirmed the underlying gap is still real -- #34 is absent from proof/ and from proof/exempt.json, and running --coverage over the whole of main's history reproduces the failure on bfe8507 ('...(#34)') -- and started writing it up as suppressing a known failure. Then I read .github/workflows/ci.yml:176, which invokes --coverage over ${{ github.event.before }}..${{ github.sha }}, not over all history. That range covered #34 only on the push that landed it. main's tip is now e5f29bf (#39), and REST shows every check run on e5f29bf completed/success. So the deleted sentence was STALE and removing it is correct. My reproduction used a range CI never uses, which is the kind of scoped measurement stated as though repo-wide that this routine is warned about -- I was about to commit it myself. Recorded, not charged. (The #34 record gap does still exist and is now written down nowhere; that is an observation for the author, not a finding against this PR.)

A third, smaller one: git's %(trailers:key=LWB-Agent) prints empty for commits a0f9481 and 46b2fd7, because their LWB-Agent line sits in a paragraph above the Co-Authored-By block and git's trailer parser only reads the last paragraph. I was ready to call those two commits untrailered. scripts/lwb_lanes.py TRAILER_RE at line 184 is a re.MULTILINE match over the whole message, not git's parser, so both commits are correctly recognised -- confirmed by lwb_lanes.py raising no trailer error for either sha. No finding.
